taylor_arch: quick thought 1 - what if we introduce a compact `pin_matrix` as a tenant->env->variant affinity table instead of lots of per-tenant pins? aim: reduce storage and make bulk edits cheaper.

alex_k: sketch please. worried about resolver perf and rollback clarity.

maria_dev: +1 on rollback clarity. compact is nice but ops need clear provenance: how do we know which write created which effective pin?

pranav_s: also need to attribute evictions/misses to a pin change in telemetry. compact encodings can hide that.

(taylor_arch posts proto sketch)

```json
{
  "pin_matrix_v1": {
    "columns": ["tenant","env","variant"],
    "rows": [
      ["acme","prod","v2:0.8;v2-canary:0.2"],
      ["acme","staging","v1"],
      ["globex","prod","v3"]
    ],
    "meta": {"created_by":"release-bot","epoch":1754328000}
  }
}
```

alex_k: compactness looks good. runtime: naive scan is O(n). we should build an index (tenant|env -> row idx) + small LRU cache for hot tenants.

maria_dev: index ok but then per-tenant state reappears. maybe keep index in a separate compact map and accept some per-tenant pointers for hot paths.

pranav_s: need scoped exceptions. e.g., tenant pinned v2, but acme/marketing needs a hard pin. propose an exceptions list keyed by (tenant, route) that overrides matrix rows.

alex_k: agree. and resolver ordering must be explicit: explicit_pin -> exceptions -> matrix -> default. make that contract clear.

maria_dev: migration options? (1) full backfill to rows, (2) lazy co-existence (resolver reads both), (3) translate on write only.

pranav_s: prefer lazy co-existence for safety. resolver checks explicit pins first, then matrix. add compat_ttl so old explicit pins expire after X days.

(taylor_arch): ok lazy co-existence. will add compat_ttl to meta. also include `created_by` and `epoch` for fast reverts.

maria_dev: telemetry fields we need: resolved_source (explicit_pin|matrix|default), matched_row_id, matrix_epoch, override_reason, referential_pin_id. include these in token-level traces.

alex_k: perf note: with index map + LRU cache median lookup ~1-2ms. cold tenants can scan; keep rows compact and prefer numeric IDs in storage to reduce IO. benchmark with 100k rows.

pranav_s: RBAC: matrix edits are powerful. require stricter write controls and UI confirmation for writes that touch >N tenants. also atomic epoch bump so rollbacks are epoch-based.

ci-bot: deploy-check: schema change detected: pin_matrix_v1. update DB migration runbook and cron backfill job if chosen.

maria_dev: can we add optional `fallback_hint` per-row to signal routing preferred cheaper variants under load? keep resolver semantics separate so fallback_hint only used by routing layer.

alex_k: fine, optional. default semantics stay simple. document separation of concerns.

(taylor_arch): next steps: draft full proto with columns, rows, meta {epoch, compat_ttl, created_by}, exceptions list, fallback_hint; implement resolver path explicit->exceptions->matrix->default; add telemetry keys; RBAC + UI warning; perf bench on staging. i'll open RFC follow-up.

pranav_s: i'll draft telemetry spec + preflight write checks to prevent accidental tenant-wide overwrites.

alex_k: i'll prototype index map + caching (in-memory trie keyed tenant|env).

maria_dev: add runbook section: quick revert via epoch rollback, and a migration cleanup job if we want to materialize legacy pins. ping infra for perf infra.

taylor_arch: thanks all, opening RFC follow-up and tagging @maria_dev @alex_k @pranav_s. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: note: thread autosaved to rfc-drafts.
